summary: Post-repair provision: Wi-Fi profile collision prevents Intune enrollment on ThinkPad T15
description: Issue summary: After depot repair (Wi-Fi module + SSD replacement) the Lenovo ThinkPad T15 fails to finish corporate provisioning. Intune enrollment stalls at 'Applying Wi-Fi profile' and the provisioning agent exits with a network profile conflict error. Impact: Blocked check-in for two devices returned from depot in the last 48 hours; users cannot complete provisioning and join corp network without manual intervention.
impact: Two devices from depot repair failed provisioning and required helpdesk manual cleanup. Affects internal provisioning SLA for depot returns and delays deskside returns to users.
timeline:
2026-03-09 10:12 - Depot completed hardware swap and pushed device to imaging pool
2026-03-09 11:03 - Imaging completed; device returned to user.
2026-03-10 08:30 - User reported provisioning stalled; ticket opened.
2026-03-11 09:15 - Helpdesk reproduced failure on staging depot machine.
2026-03-12 14:40 - Eng confirmed root cause and deployed depot script change.

steps_to_reproduce: 1) Receive device from depot after Wi-Fi module replacement
2) Run standard depot imaging (autoprov-image-v2) with corporate packages and join steps
3) Boot out-of-the-box and let provisioning agent run (provisioner v1.8)
4) Observe provisioning stall at 'Applying Wi-Fi profile' and agent exit status with "NetworkProfileApplyError: duplicate-profile-id"

2026-03-10T08:32:15Z intune-client[778]: WARN: Enrollment paused: network profile application failed

netsh wlan show profiles

investigation_notes: Helpdesk reproduced failure and captured netsh/profile output showing two profiles for 'Corp-WiFi'.

Depot imaging logs indicate that the post-image script that imports Wi-Fi XML profiles (scripts/wifi-import.sh) ran twice due to an edge-case restart when the WLAN driver enumerated after image completion.

Hypothesis: Replaced Wi-Fi module caused interface name/NetCfgInstanceId to change, triggering the wifi-import script to re-apply an already-present profile under a slightly different identifier resulting in duplicate profile metadata in the Windows WLAN store.

We also observed that if a docking station is attached during first boot the system enumerates an additional virtual interface, and the current depot script does not de-duplicate profiles by SSID, only by GUID, so duplicates were created.
No evidence of DHCP MAC duplication or network-level collision; issue isolated to local WLAN profile store and provisioning agent's strict validation.
Reproduced locally by intentionally interrupting imaging after driver install to force a re-run of wifi-import.sh; observed duplicate profile GUIDs and provisioning failure match.
Related artifact: staging depot image had older wifi-import logic that used netsh wlan add profile filename=... without checking for existing SSID - this was the immediate trigger.
comments: Helpdesk (J. Sullivan) 2026-03-10: User tech reported provisioning stuck on Wi-Fi. Collected logs and moved device back to depot for inspection.
Depot Technician (M. Lee) 2026-03-11: Reimaged device and reproduced issue. Noted 'Corp-WiFi-OLD' lingering in profiles after imaging. Suspect script ran twice post-driver install.
Eng (Diego Martinez) 2026-03-11: Investigating. Will instrument wifi-import.sh to log invocation count and skip if SSID exists.

Eng (Diego Martinez) 2026-03-12: Confirmed repro on staging. Pushed branch gh/pr/infra/1384 to add idempotency and pre-clean step (netsh wlan delete profile name="Corp-WiFi-OLD" /all) plus registry NetCfgInstanceId clear for stale entries.

Helpdesk (Aisha Kaur) 2026-03-13: Applied manual cleanup to the two affected devices (netsh wlan delete profile name="Corp-WiFi-OLD" and re-run provisioner) - enrollment completed and devices joined domain.
Depot Lead (R. Patel) 2026-03-13: Deployed updated depot image with wifi-import idempotency. Added a post-image smoke test to validate Intune enrollment completes before marking as ready.
resolution: Workaround: Helpdesk removed duplicate Wi-Fi profiles and re-ran provisioner on affected devices: commands used: 'netsh wlan delete profile name="Corp-WiFi-OLD"' and 'provisioner --enroll'.

Permanent fix: Updated wifi-import.sh in depot image to be idempotent and to clear stale NetCfg registry keys prior to profile import. PR gh/pr/infra/1384 merged and new depot image built (autoprov-image-v2.1).

Follow-up: Added a depot smoke test that verifies Intune enrollment completes within 5 minutes of imaging; updated depot runbook (confluence/redwood/depots/runbooks/wlan-cleanup) with manual steps if failure occurs.
Rollout notes: Image v2.1 deployed to central depot on 2026-03-12; regional depots scheduled for staggered rollout over next 3 days.
Closure: Affected devices were re-provisioned and validated on 2026-03-13. No further incidents reported by end of day
